title: Read this first
blocks: Shuttle Camera 0.1.31 · Installation and user guide · 18 October 2026
Capture VHS and other standard-definition sources, play movie files through HDMI, or monitor Final Cut Pro and Premiere Pro through the USB 3 Intensity Shuttle.

Development build — security changes required. The installer is unsigned; its app and extensions are ad-hoc signed and not Apple-notarized. This build requires SIP to be disabled. Apple describes disabling these checks as a temporary development measure, not a normal public-release setup. Read page 2 before deciding whether to install. Apple: testing system extensions.
An Apple-silicon Mac. This installer requires macOS 27 or later; testing was on a Mac Studio with macOS 27.0.1. Other machines and later macOS releases are not guaranteed.
A Blackmagic Intensity Shuttle USB 3, a working USB 3 cable/adapter, and administrator access. The Thunderbolt Shuttle and Intel Macs are not supported by this installer.
For VHS: a working VCR, S-Video or composite video, and red/white RCA audio cables. For output: a TV or monitor connected to the Shuttle’s HDMI OUT.
A current backup and permission to change security settings. Do not change security on a managed/work Mac without its administrator’s approval.

Shuttle Camera configures the device. Record into a separate camera app such as QuickTime Player. For movie or editor HDMI output, leave Shuttle Camera open with output started. Capture and playback share the USB interface: use one at a time.
Final Cut Pro and Premiere Pro

Screenshots show the real 0.1.31 interface with example settings. Your selected input, output device and positions may differ. This guide is independent of Blackmagic Design, Apple and Adobe; it is not their official driver documentation.

title: Security preparation
blocks: Make this decision before installing. SIP protects parts of macOS against unauthorized changes. Turning it off weakens protection across the Mac, not just this app. Developer mode relaxes extension validation. Neither setting makes downloaded software trustworthy. Apple: disabling and enabling SIP; Apple: testing system extensions.
1. Turn off SIP in Recovery — Apple silicon only
Save your work and shut down the Mac. Press and hold its power button until startup options appear. Choose Options → Continue; select an administrator and authenticate if asked.
In Recovery, choose Utilities → Terminal. Enter the command below. Follow the displayed prompts for the intended startup system, then restart normally.
These are Recovery instructions; running the command in an ordinary desktop Terminal will not complete the change. Apple: Recovery on Apple silicon.
2. Check the status in normal macOS
The installer checks for System Integrity Protection status: disabled. Do not use partial-disable flags as a substitute: this installer has not been qualified with them.
In normal macOS, open Terminal and run:

Enter your Mac administrator password; Terminal does not show password characters. This is the development configuration used during testing. It is separate from SIP. Apple: testing system extensions.

These are camera system extensions and a Core Audio plug-in, not a kernel extension. This guide does not ask you to enable third-party kernel extensions, disable FileVault, disable authenticated-root protection or globally disable Gatekeeper. Follow the specific SIP procedure rather than unrelated kext instructions.

Can SIP be turned on immediately afterwards? Do not assume this build will continue working with SIP enabled. That configuration has not been qualified, and its installer refuses installation/updates while SIP is enabled. Restore SIP when you finish testing or remove this build; page 9 explains how.

title: Install and enable
blocks: Disable external output in Premiere/Final Cut and quit those editors. Stop output and quit Shuttle Camera. Close QuickTime recording windows and other camera previews.
Open Shuttle-Capture-0.1.31.pkg. Install on the current macOS startup volume and enter your administrator password when macOS asks.

If Gatekeeper blocks the package, first verify that it came from a source you trust. Where macOS offers it, use System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway for this specific package. Do not turn off Gatekeeper globally. Apple: opening apps safely.
Let installation finish. Open Shuttle Camera from Applications. The installer preserves existing settings and backs up older Shuttle bundles.
In Terminal, type the following and drag the downloaded package into the window after the final space, then press Return:
Compare the result with the SHA256SUMS.txt supplied with this exact release:
Compare all 64 checksum characters. A matching hash detects a different file; it does not replace trusting the publisher or Apple notarization.
First installation: enable both camera extensions
In Shuttle Camera, choose Help → Driver Setup → Enable Camera.
Choose Help → Driver Setup → Enable HDMI Output if you want editor HDMI output.
If macOS asks for approval, open System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → Camera Extensions. Enable Shuttle Camera Extension and Shuttle HDMI Output Extension.
Quit and reopen Shuttle Camera after activation. Restart if macOS says a restart is required. Approve camera/microphone access for the recording app when requested.

An existing installation with both extensions already enabled does not need reactivation for the 0.1.31 interface update. First-time installation may refresh Core Audio and briefly interrupt sound; restart if the audio devices are missing.

title: Capture VHS
blocks: Capture panel. This example uses PAL composite video and 768 × 576 square-pixel output; select S-Video when using that cable.
Connect VCR video OUT to the matching Shuttle input. Connect red/white audio OUT to the Shuttle’s analog RCA inputs. Connect the Shuttle to USB 3 and press Play on the VCR.
Choose PAL or NTSC, the correct Video input, and Analog RCA. Choose a resolution and video-loss behavior, then click Apply. Close capture previews before changing settings.

In QuickTime Player, choose File → New Movie Recording. Select the Intensity Shuttle camera and Intensity Shuttle — Stereo Audio as the microphone. Check both picture and audio meter before recording.

PAL: native 720 × 576 or square-pixel 768 × 576. NTSC: native 720 × 480 or square-pixel 640 × 480. Both also offer 1280 × 960 and 1440 × 1080 (4:3). Larger sizes are scaled, with no extra tape detail. PAL 50 fps / NTSC 59.94 fps capture uses bob deinterlacing of the source fields.

On video loss: Hold last frame repeats the last picture; Black substitutes black. Dropout handling preserves the timing rather than shortening the recording, but it cannot recover a damaged tape signal. Check a short recorded clip for sound and sync before a long transfer.

title: Play a movie over HDMI
blocks: Movie file controls with illustrative settings. Example movie.mov is a placeholder; no movie was opened or played to make this screenshot.
Connect the display directly to the Shuttle’s HDMI OUT. Close all Shuttle camera previews.
Choose Video Output → Source → Movie file, then Choose movie…. Select the HDMI format.
Enable Loop to repeat the movie. Click Start output; use Stop when finished. Movie audio travels through the Shuttle; Use HDMI audio is not needed for the movie file’s own sound.

A TV may round 59.94 to “60” and 29.97 to “30”. Use Test pattern for a short display/cable test. Capture resolution and HDMI output format are separate settings. Capture cannot run at the same time as USB playback.

title: Final Cut Pro and Premiere Pro
blocks: Close Shuttle capture previews. In Shuttle Camera → Video Output choose Final Cut Pro and a format matching the timeline, for example 1080p25 for 25 fps.
Click Use HDMI audio, then Start Final Cut. Wait for Ready for Final Cut. Keep Shuttle Camera open.
In Final Cut, choose Settings → Playback → A/V Output → Intensity Shuttle — HDMI Output. Enable Window → A/V Output, then scrub and play.
When finished, turn Window → A/V Output off first; then click Stop in Shuttle Camera. Restore audio if needed. Turning A/V Output off alone does not restore the Mac’s normal sound route.
In Shuttle Camera → Video Output choose Premiere Pro and the matching HDMI format. Click Start Premiere and wait for Ready for Premiere.

In Premiere, choose Settings/Preferences → Playback. Enable Mercury Transmit and tick the video stream for Intensity Shuttle — HDMI Output. This is separate from the original Blackmagic Playback entry.
For sound, choose Intensity Shuttle — HDMI Audio in Premiere’s Audio Hardware → Default Output. The Mercury Transmit plug-in is video-only; its empty Transmit audio-stream column is expected.
Play or scrub the sequence. Leave Shuttle Camera running. If output disappears when Premiere is in the background, check Premiere’s Disable video output when in the background setting.
Disable Mercury Transmit before stopping output. If you explicitly selected the HDMI audio device in Premiere, select your normal output in Premiere Audio Hardware afterwards.
If the output device is missing

Restart Premiere after installing its plug-in. Final Cut publishes the device after the matching USB sender is ready. Start with matching timeline/output rates; conversion between arbitrary frame rates has not been qualified. The current installer places Premiere’s transmitter in the legacy Plug-ins folder used by the tested Premiere 2025 installation, not the differently named Plugins folder.
Close one editor’s external output before using another. The same physical Shuttle cannot serve two simultaneous playback sessions.

title: Sound, sync and overlays
blocks: Intensity Shuttle — Stereo Audio as the recording app’s microphone
Use HDMI audio in Shuttle Camera before starting editor output
Intensity Shuttle — HDMI Audio in Premiere Audio Hardware
Sound comes from the selected movie file

Use HDMI audio changes the Mac’s default media output and saves its previous choice. Stop, helper exit or app quit restores that choice only if the route is still Shuttle HDMI. A later manual change is respected. This does not restore an explicit per-application output selected inside Premiere; change that in Premiere itself.

Use Audio sync in Video Output while timeline monitoring. Negative values move sound earlier; positive values delay it. Range: −100 to +500 ms. If sound is slightly late, try −20 ms, press Return, and compare again. Wait about a second between adjustments. The stepper changes by 10 ms; Reset returns to zero. A live adjustment can briefly click or skip. This setting is for timeline HDMI sound, not capture recording.
Timecode: TC HH:MM:SS:FF from the editor, with a DF marker for drop-frame. Dashes mean valid timecode was not supplied. It is not an invented elapsed counter.
L/R audio meters: independent stereo levels with peak hold and clip indication. The meters show sound sent to HDMI.
Positions: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right, top centre or bottom centre. Timecode and meters have separate positions.
Title safe (80%) / Action safe (90%): optional white/yellow guides. These are the app’s guide percentages, not a guarantee of compliance with a broadcaster’s delivery specification.

Overlays affect the outgoing HDMI picture only; they do not burn into the source file or editor project. Settings are saved and update live. Timecode is available for editor output; meters and safe guides also work with movie playback.

Shuttle Camera → About shows the version; Quit (⌘Q) closes the app. Help → Output Setup gives source-specific instructions. Help → Diagnostics opens the technical log. Help → Driver Setup contains the extension enable/disable actions.

title: Troubleshooting and limits
blocks: Quit both editors and Shuttle Camera, close capture previews, check SIP status, and use the current startup volume. Installer → Window → Installer Log shows the precise reason.
Use Help → Driver Setup → Enable Camera. Approve Camera Extensions in System Settings, then reopen Shuttle Camera and the recording app.
Use the separate Stereo Audio microphone, Analog RCA for VCR red/white cables, and check app microphone permission.
Close capture previews, check USB 3 cable/adapter and power, reconnect the Shuttle after stopping clients, then retry. Read Help → Diagnostics.
Restart Premiere; confirm the Shuttle transmitter exists in the Plug-ins path on page 9. Do not select Blackmagic Playback as a substitute for this plug-in.
Check Premiere Audio Hardware or Final Cut’s Use HDMI audio route. TV speakers must be enabled; HDMI-to-DVI connections do not provide TV audio.
On the tested Dell P2213t with HDMI-to-DVI, set its Input Color Format to YPbPr. RGB selection in this app is not implemented. Direct HDMI to the tested TV worked.
Click Restore audio or choose normal speakers in Sound settings. Also undo any explicit HDMI output selection inside Premiere.
Disable external output, then stop Shuttle output. Relaunch only after saving work. Report the format, editor version and Diagnostics log; do not keep toggling output during a hung session.

This build is Apple silicon only. Capture is standard-definition; S-Video/composite VHS capture is the main tested workflow. Listed Component/HDMI capture options do not imply HD capture support. There is no DaVinci Resolve output integration, selectable RGB HDMI mode, simultaneous capture/playback or qualified 1080p50/60 output.

Testing covered the listed PAL/NTSC/1080 modes on one Mac Studio setup. It is not proof of compatibility with every USB controller, display, movie codec, editor update or tape. Very long sessions, exact measured physical A/V latency and fresh installs on other Macs have not been comprehensively qualified.

For a useful report, include the app/macOS/editor versions, source and HDMI format, connection type, whether the camera is in use, and relevant Diagnostics/Installer Log lines. Review logs for private file names before sharing them.

title: Remove it and restore security
blocks: Save your work. Disable editor external output, quit the editors, stop Shuttle output and restore normal audio. Close recording/camera previews.
In Shuttle Camera, use Help → Driver Setup → Disable Camera. In System Settings → Camera Extensions, turn off both Shuttle extensions.
Move Shuttle Camera.app from Applications to the Bin using Finder. Allow macOS to remove its bundled extensions if prompted. Do not manually delete files from /Library/SystemExtensions.

In Finder → Go → Go to Folder, visit the HAL path below and move only Shuttle Audio.driver to the Bin. Visit the Premiere path and move only Shuttle Transmit.bundle to the Bin. Administrator approval may be required.
Restart to unload audio and finish any pending extension removal. Check that other audio devices work normally. Do not use systemextensionsctl reset; it would affect unrelated extensions.
Turn extension developer mode off in normal macOS
Turn SIP back on in Recovery

Boot to Recovery as on page 2, choose Utilities → Terminal, run the command below, then restart normally. Verify with csrutil status in the desktop Terminal. If you separately changed Startup Security policies, consult Apple’s Recovery guidance to restore the appropriate policy for your startup system. Apple: disabling and enabling SIP.

The ad-hoc development extensions may stop working after restoring SIP; do not treat this as a supported way to keep using this build. Retain backups until you have checked your files and normal audio. Accessing installer backups may require administrator rights.
